fear_greed.commentary: Fear & Greed sits at 17, still in extreme fear, despite Monday's rally; it is down from 26 a week ago and about level with a month ago.

markets.summary: A violent rebound on Monday: the S&P 500 jumped 4.73% to 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq surged 6.51% to 24,089.56, both their best days since April 2025, while the Dow gained 3.01% to 49,595.31. The trigger was Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, sending the stock up 31.5% to $165.05. Despite the bounce, all three indexes remain below their 40-week averages with RSI in the low 40s. Small caps joined in, with the Russell 2000 up 3.4% to 2,669.66, and the 10-year Treasury yield was little changed near 4.92%. Gold futures rose 3.9% to about $3,651 and silver futures 5.2% to about $43.15, but both remain well below their 40-week averages. Breadth improved to 52.2% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average, still neutral, while Fear & Greed remains in extreme fear.

weather.summary: A large, cold high pressure system dominates the Plains, Midwest and South, bringing lake-effect snow to the Great Lakes tonight and the season's first freeze to parts of the Southern Plains Tuesday night. Pacific fronts keep rain and mountain snow coming to the Pacific Northwest and northern California, while a low developing south of Florida Wednesday brings strengthening onshore winds to the Southeast and a heavy-rain threat for the Carolina coast by evening.
